en: Models, large language models, they generate
text, or technically they generate tokens,
but that leads to text in the end.
Now, you can also use large language models
to generate structured outputs, which is
still text, to be honest, but not text meant
for humans, but for example, for machines.
Now, that does not matter if you are using
ChatGPT or Claude or Microsoft Copilot, but
it may matter if you're building some
software, on top of AI. For example, let's
say you're building some software that
should analyze incoming emails and then
allow your program to either store them or
forward them. To make that decision, you
need some structured data that has always
the same predefined shape so that your
program, which is not AI, can act on that
data and continue appropriately.
That's why you can, of course, simply ask
models to return data in a certain So for
example, in something called the JSON
format, which looks like this,
but which is also why all these model
providers nowadays
typically offer some structured output mode
if you
use them programmatically to ensure that
what you get back from the model
is still text, but not text for humans,
instead for machines. That's what structured
outputs refer to.
